audit_items.title: Verify Fork Digest Computation: Is compute_fork_digest correctly implemented to derive the expected digest for each epoch?

phase1_summary.implementation_notes: compute_fork_digest takes current_version and genesis_validators_root, computes fork_data_root and returns first 4 bytes. compute_fork_digest_fulu (Fulu fork) also XORs with blob parameters hash.

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: Fork digest must be deterministic given same inputs
potential_issues: Fulu fork digest includes blob parameters hashing with toBytesLE (little-endian) encoding
Epoch and MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK encoded in 16-byte buffer then hashed
phase2_analysis.risk_areas: Cross-client consensus if byte encoding differs

phase3_verdict.rationale: Implementation follows spec but Fulu fork digest XOR mechanism with blob parameters requires cross-client verification to ensure identical encoding (little-endian uint64). The use of toBytesLE is correct for spec compliance but should be validated against reference tests.
recommendations: Verify test vectors for compute_fork_digest_fulu exist and pass
Cross-check encoding with other CL clients (Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Lodestar)

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the CL implement timeout handling for Engine API calls when EL returns SYNCING status?

phase1_summary.implementation_notes: Engine API has explicit timeouts: engineApiConnectionTimeout=5s, web3RequestsTimeout=8s. DataProviderTimeout exception raised on timeout. Counters track timeouts via engine_api_timeouts metric.

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: CL must not block indefinitely on EL API calls
findings: Explicit timeout constants defined (5s connection, 8s request)
AsyncTimeoutError caught and converted to DataProviderTimeout
Degraded state set on timeout with hysteresis counter
Metrics track timeout events

phase3_verdict.rationale: Nimbus implements robust timeout handling for Engine API. All requests use configurable timeouts, failures trigger degraded state transitions, and metrics provide observability. The timeout mechanism prevents indefinite blocking.
phase3_verdict.evidence: Lines 54-58 define engineApiConnectionTimeout and web3RequestsTimeout. Line 239 raises DataProviderTimeout on AsyncTimeoutError.

audit_items.title: Verify CL resilience: Can the CL continue processing attestations and block proposals while Engine API calls are pending or timing out?

phase1_summary.implementation_notes: Nimbus uses async/await architecture (chronos). Engine API calls are async futures with timeouts. noCancel wrapper used in some cases.

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: CL consensus duties must not be blocked by EL API calls
findings: Async architecture allows concurrent operation
Timeouts prevent indefinite blocking
Need to verify attestation/proposal paths are independent

phase3_verdict.rationale: Architecture supports async operation but full verification requires tracing attestation and proposal duty paths to confirm they don't share blocking dependencies with Engine API calls.
recommendations: Trace attestation duty execution path
Trace block proposal execution path
Verify no shared locks or blocking queues with EL communication

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: Proposer must be deterministically derived and cryptographically bound

Slot mixed into hash buffer
Effective balance used in selection
Block signature binds proposer identity

audit_items.title: Verify Validator Assignment Integrity: Can a validator deny or falsely claim proposer duty assignment?

phase1_summary.implementation_notes: Proposer lookahead is deterministic and publicly verifiable from beacon state

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: Validators cannot manipulate their selection or falsely claim proposer status
findings: Lookahead derived from immutable state data
Signature verification prevents false claims
RANDAO contribution is committed before selection

phase3_verdict.rationale: Proposer selection uses deterministic algorithm from committed state. Validators cannot influence their own selection retroactively. Block signatures prevent false claims as they require the actual proposer's private key.
phase3_verdict.evidence: compute_proposer_index uses state-derived seed and indices

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Is the MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD delay sufficient to prevent same-epoch randao manipulation of proposer assignments?

phase1_summary.implementation_notes: MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD is a preset constant (typically 1 epoch). Used in get_seed computation to ensure lookahead delay.

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: Lookahead delay prevents same-epoch randao manipulation
findings: MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD enforces delay between randao contribution and use
Proposer selection uses seed from past epoch
Spec-mandated constant value

phase3_verdict.rationale: MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD is correctly implemented as per consensus spec. The delay ensures randao contributions cannot immediately influence proposer selection, preventing same-epoch manipulation attacks.
phase3_verdict.evidence: Constant defined in presets, used in helpers.nim get_seed function

audit_items.title: Supporting Node Check: Verify validator randao contributions cannot be withheld or replayed to influence proposer selection

phase1_summary.implementation_notes: RANDAO reveal required in block, mixed into state randao_mixes

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: RANDAO cannot be withheld or replayed
findings: RANDAO reveal is mandatory in block
Missing reveal = invalid block
Replay prevented by domain separation and epoch binding

phase3_verdict.rationale: RANDAO reveal is mandatory in each block. Withholding means not proposing (validator misses slot). Replay is prevented by epoch-specific domain in signature. Implementation follows spec.
phase3_verdict.evidence: Block validation requires valid RANDAO reveal signature

phase2_analysis.invariant_check: Proposer indices must be from active set
findings: Function takes indices: seq[ValidatorIndex] which is pre-filtered active set
compute_proposer_index samples from this filtered list
Inactive validators cannot be selected

phase3_verdict.rationale: compute_proposer_indices only samples from the provided indices parameter, which is populated with active validators. The function cannot return indices outside this set.

phase3_verdict.rationale: Active validator filtering uses standard is_active_validator check which excludes validators where exit_epoch <= current_epoch.

phase3_verdict.rationale: While is_active_validator checks exit_epoch, the slashed flag exclusion from proposer selection needs explicit verification. Per spec, slashed validators can remain active but should not propose.
recommendations: Verify slashed validator handling in compute_proposer_index
Check if effective_balance is zeroed for slashed validators

audit_items.title: Verify Not-Yet-Activated Validators Are Excluded from Proposer Selection

phase3_verdict.rationale: is_active_validator function explicitly checks activation_epoch <= epoch. Validators pending activation have activation_epoch > current_epoch and are excluded.
